newsitem.title: USA: N.E. Electric sees 620 early retirements.
newsitem.headline: N.E. Electric sees 620 early retirements.

text.p: New England Electric System vice president of human resources said Tuesday he expects around 620 of the company's unionized and managerial staff to take an early retirement package.

The company signed a deal late Monday with two unions, which in addition to a December deal with a third union and plans for management, will cut its 4,900 workforce by around 12 percent, said David Kennedy, vice president of human resources.

The retirement deal was offered in expectations the new owners of its electric generating plants, up for sale, will require fewer workers. NEES will also need fewer non-union, administrative employees after the sale, Kennedy said.

NEES will also offer a severance package to its unionized workers who will lose their jobs as a result of the sale of the plants, Kennedy said. But the company did not know how many workers would be offered the package, he said.
Kennedy said the costs associated with the early retirement and severance package will be part of its deregulation transition costs, most of which are expected to be passed on to customers in rates.
